va_silver_fortune_boulder.blurb: A bouldering stop in the Guest River Gorge of Southwest Virginia, tucked into the Mile Two stretch. The block is short but stretched out lengthwise, with steep faces on every side and generally friendly landings. Fourteen problems run from V0 up to V7: a handful of easy and moderate lines in the V0 to V4 range, then a harder cluster at V6 and V7 for stronger climbers. Look for it beside the trail on the left, just beyond the Rapid Boulder and the Big Boulder. Crash pads are the expected protection, and it works well as one stop on a longer gorge bouldering day.

va_vision_boulder.blurb: A big, standalone block in the Mile Two section of Guest River Gorge, Southwest Virginia, sitting beneath the Machine Gun Area. All four sides carry lines, and the stone is tall enough for satisfying problems without becoming a true highball, with an easy way down off the top. Fourteen boulder problems span V0 to V6, weighted toward the easy and moderate end (mostly V0 to V4), which makes it a good pick for a mixed group. The holds are varied and interesting from one face to the next. Bring pads.

va_lower_god_s_area.blurb: A compact collection of climbs along the foot of the God's Area on Old Rag, inside Shenandoah National Park. This is mainly a trad venue, with a couple of bolted sport lines mixed in, and the grades stretch from 5.7 through the 5.12 range; the harder end (5.11 and 5.12) accounts for more than half of the fourteen routes. Expect steep faces with thin, sustained edges and cracks, plus the Bushwhack Corridor. It is a lesser-visited, serious little crag rather than a beginner spot, so plan on being comfortable with gear and route-finding on a faint path.

va_browns_island.blurb: A small urban climbing spot on the north bank of the James River in downtown Richmond, directly across from the Manchester Wall. The climbing is on tall concrete pillars, roughly 60 feet high, split by elevated train tracks. The north pillar is the easy one to reach; the south pillar stands partly in the water and is best visited when the river is low. Most of the fourteen routes are bolted sport lines, with a couple of trad climbs and one top-rope, and the grades cluster around 5.10 with some 5.11 and one 5.12. Climbs can be found in either sun or shade, and the pillars must be led to reach the anchors.

va_horizon_boulder.blurb: The most recognisable block in the Horizon Area of Grayson Highlands State Park, high in the mountains of Southwest Virginia. After a stiff uphill walk the boulder cluster appears, and this massive stone is the largest one on the right side of the group. The surface is mostly smooth: grippy in cool weather but noticeably greasy when it warms up. Fourteen problems range from beginner-friendly lines around VB to V2 up to a few hard testpieces in the V6 to V9 range, including one of the park's best-known lines. Ponies and long views come with the setting.
